newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures reverses to end weaker.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures reverses to end weaker.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures pared gains to end weaker on Thursday after trading narrowly ahead of U.S. trade data and the Group of Seven (G7) summit.

Dealers said activity was flat and the trading band disappointingly narrow with players taking a cautious attitude. The lead Nikkei 225 September contract slipped 120 points to 20,455, drifting close to the intraday low of 20,410.
"Possibly smaller players were in the market but it was trading sideways most of the time," said one dealer.
The contract should next test near-term support at 20,400 points, and after that 20,300, he said.
Nikkei futures found scarce inspiration from relatively flat Tokyo stocks and yen currency fluctuations, dealers said.
In the absence of trade factors, technicals were seen likely to drive prices within a 400 to 500-point band.

Dealers said the U.S. trade deficit, forecast in a Reuter poll to widen to $10 billion in April -- following a $8.51 billion deficit in March -- could renew pressure on Japan to close its trade gap with the United States.
The Taiwan futures contract for June also slipped 4.0 points to 368, after hitting new highs at 374.4 earlier.
